one_liner: Zig/WASM polygon booleans and rounded buffer for web GIS; 2.7-3.3x faster than native GEOS on a 4,040-parcel union.
what_it_does: qdgeo does five planar polygon operations: union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference and a signed rounded buffer. Any boolean can also buffer its result in the same call. It ships as a 135 KB (50.8 KB gzipped) import-free WASM module with an ESM JavaScript binding (geo.union, geo.difference, geo.buffer, ...) that exchanges flat Float64Array coordinates plus ring/polygon end offsets, the layout OpenLayers and deck.gl already use. A native Zig API is allocator-explicit (unionAll, boolean, buffer) and reads and writes WKB. A native shared library exports the same flat and WKB C ABI. It is not a GEOS replacement: polygon output only, no predicates, no repair and no precision model.
how_it_is_fast: The overlay is a single Martinez-Rueda sweep line. It uses per-layer winding counts instead of in/out parity (no edge-type classification), orders events lexicographically by (x, y) as a symbolic shear so vertical edges need no special case, and calls exact adaptive orientation predicates at every sign decision. Events are stored structure-of-arrays with order-preserving u128 sort keys, bucketed by x and pdq-sorted within buckets, and the sweep processes all events at one point as a batch. The buffer follows the JTS/GEOS construction: one raw self-intersecting offset curve per ring, line or point, resolved in one overlay pass by keeping regions with winding depth at least 1. The result-vertex hash map is pre-sized to its upper bound with a cheap custom hash. There is no snap-rounding ladder: a failed labelling is retried once with a graph relabelling and once with re-noding, otherwise an error is returned. The WASM build enables simd128.
when_to_use: Browser or Node web-GIS apps (OpenLayers, deck.gl, MapLibre, Leaflet) that need union/difference/buffer client-side: GEOS has no supported browser build, and qdgeo was 7-28x faster than JSTS, Turf and polyclip-ts on the author's parcel suite

Unioning or buffering many adjacent cadastral parcels with hairline gaps and shared boundaries: the full 4,040-parcel union took 160 ms (WASM) or 130 ms (native) vs 426 ms for GEOS 3.13.1, and qdgeo was one of only two engines returning correct geometry there
Pipelines that would rather get an error than snapped or approximated geometry: qdgeo's disputed vertices matched exact rational reconstruction (0 m error) where GEOS was off by up to 7.2e-5 m
Small-download constraints: 50.8 KB gzipped vs about 778 KB for geos-wasm (which was not benchmarked)
when_not_to_use: Very large single polygons: on a 19,208-coordinate parcel GEOS buffered +2 m in 8.25 ms vs 33.2 ms (about 4x faster), and 13.0 vs 31.9 ms for -2 m

Dirty or invalid input you expect the library to fix: qdgeo rejects zero-area or degenerate rings and failed noding instead of repairing them (6 of 161 JTS buffer assertions fail for this reason). Run make_valid/ST_MakeValid or GeoRepair first

Workloads that need an answer for every valid input: 4 of 3,946 adjacent-parcel cluster unions return an error because f64 cannot hold the crossing. Smaller batches make this more likely (4 failures at 250-parcel batches, 0 at 500-1,000)

C++ codebases wanting a native library: the core is Zig 0.16, no C header ships, and the native shared library's C ABI (global result block, single-threaded, non-reentrant, errors printed to stderr) is described as built for differential benchmarks

Anything beyond five areal operations (predicates, line/point outputs, simplification, spatial indexes, CRS handling), or projects that need maturity: first commit 2026-09-14, 0 stars, not published to npm (registry returns 404)

integration.dependencies: none (pure Zig, no C or C++, WASM declares no imports); the comparison suite needs Python 3.13, Shapely/GEOS, Rust 1.88+ and npm engines
integration.min_toolchain: Zig 0.16.0 (minimum_zig_version); JS consumers need an ESM bundler or Node, and the harness used Node 22+
integration.platforms: wasm32-freestanding with simd128 (browsers, Node, workers; heap capped at 512 MiB), plus any native target Zig builds (static library, or shared libqdgeo_native with a C ABI)
integration.thread_safety: The flat and WKB host ABI is documented as single-threaded and non-reentrant: one global input block and one global result block, reused across calls. The native Zig API takes an explicit allocator and returns arena-owned Geometry values; its concurrency is not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it covers GEOS/Shapely union_all, intersection, difference, symmetric_difference and buffer for polygons (WKB in and out natively), but with a different API, no precision model or repair, and polygon-only results

gotchas: ABI status 5 means both 'malformed geometry' and 'valid but not representable in f64'. The failure is deterministic, so retrying does nothing, but nudging or rounding the input usually moves past it
Coordinates are planar in input units and no CRS is read from WKB: reproject lon/lat to a metric CRS before asking for metre buffers

Buffering several polygons buffers their union, and a zero-distance buffer still runs union and normalisation rather than returning a copy. Output limits are checked after construction, not enforced as an allocation budget
The shipped WASM is ReleaseSafe (runtime safety checks on). ReleaseFast is 11% faster with bit-identical output if you build it yourself
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick qdgeo over clipper2next/Clipper2 or CavalierContours when the target is the browser or you need exact, unsnapped output on GIS parcels rather than integer-lattice C++ clipping. Pair it with GeoRepair, which handles the invalid-geometry repair qdgeo refuses, and use TG for fast point-in-polygon/intersects predicates, which qdgeo does not offer.
verified_claims_summary: The author's comparison suite (tests/compare, Zig 0.16.0 ReleaseSafe, Node 22+) ran 26 union and buffer workloads on a 4,040-parcel, 135,080-coordinate public GeoMoose dataset. Each figure is the median of three suite runs of 11 repeats, on one unnamed idle machine. Against GEOS 3.13.1 via Shapely 2.1.2, the full union took 160 ms (WASM) and 130 ms (native) vs 426 ms (2.7x and 3.3x, derived from page data; the README rounds this to '3.1x native GEOS'). The geometric mean over all 26 workloads has native GEOS 1.5x slower than qdgeo WASM (1.36-1.62 across runs), and GEOS wins on the 19,208-coordinate single-parcel buffer. Boundaries differ: GEOS times the operation only on prebuilt GEOS objects, while qdgeo native includes a WKB parse and encode round trip. GEOS itself measured 417 ms and 356 ms an hour apart, so gaps under about 20% are unresolved.
status_note: Brand-new (first commit 2026-09-14, last 2026-09-23, 15 commits, 0 stars) and actively developed by one author under MIT, with CI running unit tests, WASM checks and the JTS suite. The 'experimental' label was removed on 2026-09-16, but it has no npm release yet, so install it from git or vendor the WASM artifact.
